note: Set B is more accurate on specific engineering data points (peak lift-to-drag ratios), whereas Set A makes numerous factually incorrect claims about trends (asserting 'increasing' over ranges where the curves clearly peak and decline due to stall). Set A also misreads specific values like drag coefficient at high lift. Set B contains duplicate claims and misses axis range context, but has significantly fewer factual errors.
remarks: Both sets incorrectly state the max lift coefficient for SNL-FFA-W3-500 as 2.0 (graph shows ~1.6). Set A's trend claims are systematically flawed because they ignore stall behavior (e.g., claiming lift increases up to 20 deg when it stalls around 15 deg). Set B has redundant claims for FFA-W3-360 and FFA-W3-211 lift-to-drag ratios.
